solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pentagon's in regular form, as fever is breaking out all around 25?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go all around the Latin word, enclosing it
breaking out suggests the letters of fever and is bursting loose and regrouping

parts.note: qua is Latin for 'as' or 'in the capacity of', used in English too

explanation.surface: A doctor wonders whether a feverish rash spreading round a patient looks oddly pentagonal.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing '25?' is a second hint: twenty-five is five squared. It points at the number, not at the entry 25-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-square is an old adjective for a figure with five equal sides, which is what a regular pentagon has.

clue.text: To keep from sustenance is not that much of a mishap

indicators.note: the answer is only part of these words, not the whole lot, so it lies concealed within them

explanation.surface: Going without food is said to be not such a calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve someone, depriving them of food, is the archaic verb sense here.

clue.text: Councillor of state that's repeatedly suppressing king

indicators.note: in a down clue, suppressing means sitting on top of, so the king goes below

parts.note: viz is the abbreviation of videlicet, meaning that is
repeatedly says 'that's' is given a second time, as ie, also meaning that is
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A state councillor keeps holding down the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high official or minister in Muslim states, advising the ruler.

clue.text: Senor's enthralling discussion, bound to lead on to inspiration for one writing words of love song

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the abbreviation wraps round everything else

parts.note: Sr is the abbreviation for Senor

indicators.note: lead on to says the first piece is followed by the next

parts.note: a moot is a debate or discussion
to bound is to hop or leap

parts.words: inspiration for one writing words of love
parts.note: Erato is the Muse of love poetry, inspiring lyric writers

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman's talk leaps to the Muse who inspires a romantic lyricist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love song' looks like the definition, but 'love' belongs to Erato's description; the definition is just 'song'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sade's 1984 hit of this title is a well-known pop number, so it is a song.

clue.text: Provincial master in trouble, having broken short bone

indicators.note: having broken into means the shortened bone is split open to take the other letters
short means the bone's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the ulna is a bone of the forearm

indicators.note: in trouble suggests master is disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster from the provinces gets into a mess after fracturing a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland, so a provincial here is a man from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is one of Ireland's four provinces, so a native of it is a provincial.

clue.text: Take a sweet drink to accompany a yoghurty dish

indicators.note: to accompany says the following piece comes along next

parts.note: R, from Latin recipe, is the prescription abbreviation for take
it is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Have a sweet drink alongside a yoghurt-based dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is the Indian side of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs, served with curry.

clue.text: Lab has denied origins down in Paris

indicators.note: both words lose their origins, the first letters, so L and H are taken away

explanation.surface: A laboratory in a French city has been refused permission to go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A bas is the French cry 'down with', so it is how 'down' is said in Paris.

clue.text: Visit from outer space to wrap reportedly new jersey for blue-eyed boy?

indicators.note: to wrap means the first phrase goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: aliens in science fiction beam in to visit
NJ is the abbreviation for the US state New Jersey

explanation.surface: An alien visitor wraps a boy in a new pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' excuses the lower case: 'new jersey' is the US state as said, not written. 'jersey' looks like a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin was the youngest and favourite son of Jacob, so a family's pet child is called one.

clue.text: Rock solid apprentice reporter initially finding work at New York Times

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of solid, apprentice and reporter

parts.note: a do is an activity or piece of business
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A dependable trainee journalist lands a job at a major American newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock solid' looks like one phrase, but 'Rock' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonyx is a banded onyx stone, a variety of chalcedony mineral.

clue.text: NHS freeloading is criminal but offence is not taken

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, twisted out of order

explanation.surface: Sponging off the health service is a crime, though nobody is upset about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock reassurance that a slight has been forgiven and no grudge is held.

clue.text: Moderately irritated by mozzies, is deserting

indicators.note: irritated suggests the remaining letters are stirred up and rearranged
is deserting means the letters I and S leave the word mozzies

explanation.surface: Someone bitten by mosquitoes is only mildly annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deserting' removes I and S from MOZZIES, leaving MOZZE, which 'irritated' rearranges. 'Mozzies' is Australian and British slang for mosquitoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mezzo is the musical direction meaning half or moderately, as in mezzo forte.

clue.text: Keeping close to Usain, his incredible strength gets man over the line

indicators.note: the combined letters keep, or hold inside, the chosen letter
incredible suggests his letters are rearranged beyond belief

parts.note: power is strength

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of Usain

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt's amazing power carries him across the finish line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the line' looks like a sprint finish, but a line is also a shipping company, and the man over it owns its vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipping line is run by a ship-owning boss, a person in charge of a fleet of vessels.

clue.text: Scene in which heart's moved, nursing little baby

indicators.note: nursing means holding something inside, as a nurse holds a child
the middle letters of the word for scene have one of them shifted, swapping their order

parts.note: a site is a scene or place
wee is Scottish and informal for little

explanation.surface: A tender scene in which someone is cradling a tiny infant and feeling emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart's moved' swaps the two middle letters of the word for scene before the little word goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby is an affectionate term for a loved one, just like the endearment sweetie.

clue.text: North American house with rumoured 50 Cent entrée?

indicators.note: entrée means the first part enters ahead, coming before the other piece
rumoured means we take what is said rather than written

parts.note: 50 Cent is a US hip-hop artist, that is, a rapper

explanation.surface: An American home is said to have the singer 50 Cent coming through its front door.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound-alike only works in a non-rhotic (British) accent, where the final R of 'a rapper' is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native people of the Great Plains, so one of them is a North American.

clue.text: 'Oops!' said, maybe, abruptly clumped?

indicators.note: clumped suggests letters bundled together in a heap and rearranged
abruptly means the word maybe is cut off short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A clumsy person tumbles and somebody exclaims in sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abruptly' cuts MAYBE to MAYB, which joins OOPS and SAID for 'clumped' to rearrange. The whole clue also describes the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: This nursery exclamation is what an adult says to a toddler who has just fallen with a thump.

clue.text: I refuse to accept edited copy for one seeking favour

indicators.note: to accept means taking the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: shan't is a refusal: I shall not

indicators.note: edited copy is text reworked, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer won't take on the revised text for a client looking for approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady flatters people in power to win their goodwill, which is seeking favour.

clue.text: Play guitar outside of training college range

indicators.note: outside of means the playing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings
PE is physical education, training at school

explanation.surface: A student strums a guitar outside a teacher-training college.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full spread of values, so it is a range.

clue.text: Flash inset for notice that's different typeface?

indicators.note: inset means placed inside the rearranged word
different tells us the letters of notice are put in another order

parts.note: a flash is a moment, informally a mo

explanation.surface: A printer inserts a flashy notice in a different font.
explanation.walkthrough: 'typeface' looks like a font, but here it is a face made from typed characters.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley built from keyboard characters is literally a face of type.

clue.text: One repeatedly firing piece of American bread

parts.note: someone who pumps bullets out shot after shot is a pumper
a nickel is an American five-cent piece

explanation.surface: A gunman blazes away with a fragment of a US weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a gun to go with the firing, but it is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dark, dense German rye loaf, a kind of bread.

clue.text: Twittering judge's lead for now restraining golden retriever?

indicators.note: restraining means the two letters hold something between them
lead means the first letters of judge and now

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship, which retrieved the Golden Fleece

explanation.surface: A judge's dog lead restrains a golden retriever for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golden retriever' looks like a dog, but it is Jason's ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Twittering is chatter of birds, and incomprehensible chatter is gibberish or specialist talk.

clue.text: Suddenly get angry on gaining access to the kids?

indicators.note: gaining access to means getting inside the other piece

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or children
re means on, concerning, as in email subjects

explanation.surface: A divorced parent flares up when finally allowed to see their children.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose your temper all of a sudden is an idiom, as a bull charging at a red cape.

clue.text: Old ____ used it to slash, and copper's rubbed ____ in wound

indicators.note: in, with rubbed, says the turned word is rubbed into the other piece

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the 's adds S

indicators.note: wound, as in wound round, means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: the missing word in both blanks is salt, from the phrase old salt

explanation.surface: An old sailor wielded a weapon, and the policeman added insult to injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Both blanks hide the same word: 'old salt' is a veteran sailor, and 'rub salt in the wound' an idiom for making a hurt worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is the short, broad-bladed sword that sailors carried for slashing.

clue.text: Riddle: divide fourth prime by first square and subtract any number

indicators.note: subtract means take away the letter for an unspecified number
divide means split open the number to put something inside

parts.note: the primes run 2, 3, 5, 7, so the fourth is seven
the first square number is one, written as Roman I
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle: do some division with primes and squares, then take something away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle, matching the maths, but it is the coarse sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large coarse sieve for soil or grain, so both are sifting tools.

clue.text: Hefty feller, US writer, receives open country kiss

indicators.note: receives means the writer's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
a lea is open grassland or meadow
X is the conventional letter for a kiss

explanation.surface: A burly lumberjack, actually an American author, is greeted in a meadow with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like a big man but is something that fells: an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A poleaxe is a heavy axe used to fell cattle or in battle, a hefty felling tool.

clue.text: For me, maybe, Tommy Cooper with side-splitting larks, that's hysterical

indicators.note: hysterical suggests the letters are thrown into wild disorder
the sides of larks split off, leaving only its middle letters

explanation.surface: The comedian Tommy Cooper's side-splitting larks are hysterically funny.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Cooper was a much-loved British comedy magician. The Who's 'Tommy' is the definition, and 'For me, maybe' has a work speaking of a type that includes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy, by The Who, is the best-known example of a stage musical built from rock music.

clue.text: Not a queen for backing the country?

indicators.note: backing means the remaining letters run backwards
not a means the letter A is removed from the word

parts.note: regina is Latin for queen, seen in Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone declines to support the monarch and sides with the nation instead.
explanation.walkthrough: REGINA without A is REGIN, which 'backing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked nation in West Africa, so it is one example of a country.

clue.text: Former Aussie rockers cut short by maiden, a cheeky young thing

parts.note: M is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: cut short means the band's name loses its final letter

parts.note: INXS were an Australian rock band, now disbanded

explanation.surface: Retired Australian rock stars are upstaged by a sassy girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A pert, impudent girl is described as a saucy little hussy, which is exactly a minx.

clue.text: In Wetherspoon establishment at opening, non-boozer is first to be rejected

indicators.note: in says the following pieces go inside the initials

parts.note: J D Wetherspoon is the British pub chain, named with the initials JD

indicators.note: at opening means the first letter of establishment

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker
first is number one

explanation.surface: In a pub chain, the teetotaller is the first customer thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Wetherspoon's is a big British pub chain whose full name is J D Wetherspoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo thrown overboard has been discarded, and to reject something is likewise to cast it off.
